title: Beti Hai Anmol Yojana Himachal Pradesh
meta_description: Beti Hai Anmol Yojana gives Rs 10,000 FD at birth and scholarships to girl children of BPL families in HP. Eligibility, benefits, and how to apply.

hero.one_liner: Beti Hai Anmol Yojana gives a Rs 10,000 fixed deposit at birth plus class-wise scholarships to girl children of BPL families in Himachal Pradesh.

what_is_it: The Beti Hai Anmol Yojana is a Himachal Pradesh government scheme designed to promote the welfare of the girl child in families that live below the poverty line (BPL). The scheme provides two types of financial support: a one-time Rs 10,000 fixed deposit created in the name of the girl child at birth, and annual scholarships for her education from Class 1 through Class 12.

The Rs 10,000 fixed deposit is opened in the name of the girl child at birth or within one year of birth by the Women and Child Development Department; the amount is deposited in a post office savings account or a government-designated bank account in the girl's name. She can withdraw the accumulated amount along with interest when she turns 18 years of age, providing a small but meaningful financial resource for her marriage, higher education, or entrepreneurship.

Apply via the anganwadi worker or Child Development Project Officer. Family must hold a BPL card and be an HP resident.

how_to_apply.title: Register the Birth
how_to_apply.description: Get the girl child's birth registered at the Gram Panchayat or municipal authority immediately after birth; the birth certificate is a mandatory document for enrolling in the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana and must be obtained before applying.

how_to_apply.title: Contact the Anganwadi Worker
how_to_apply.description: Approach the Anganwadi worker in your area within one year of the girl's birth; the worker will provide you with the Beti Hai Anmol application form, explain the BPL certificate requirement, and help you complete the registration process.

how_to_apply.title: Submit Documents at Block ICDS Office
how_to_apply.description: Submit the application form along with the girl's birth certificate, the family's BPL ration card or income certificate, parent's Aadhaar cards, HP domicile certificate, and a bank passbook or post office savings account details in the girl's name.

how_to_apply.title: FD is Opened by the Department
how_to_apply.description: After verification, the Women and Child Development Department opens a Rs 10,000 fixed deposit in the girl's name at the designated bank or post office; the family receives acknowledgement of the FD and can track it through the issuing institution.

how_to_apply.title: Annual Scholarship Renewal
how_to_apply.description: Each year, submit a school attendance certificate and promotion certificate to the block ICDS office to claim the annual scholarship for the current class; the scholarship is credited to the family's bank account after verification of the school documents.

ministry: Women and Child Development Department, Himachal Pradesh

extra_sections.heading: What Beti Hai Anmol Yojana Is
content: The scholarship component of the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana supports the girl child's education by providing annual scholarships from Class 1 through Class 12; the amounts range from Rs 450 per year in Class 1 to 3, rising to Rs 1,200 per year in Classes 11 and 12. This progressive structure gives higher support as the girl advances to senior secondary level, where out-of-pocket education expenses such as textbooks, stationery, and school fees tend to increase.

The scheme covers a maximum of two girl children per BPL family; if a family has more than two daughters, only the first two are covered. This two-child limit is consistent with Himachal Pradesh's family planning guidelines and ensures that the scheme's finite budget is focused on encouraging smaller families to invest in their daughters' welfare.

extra_sections.heading: What Beti Hai Anmol Yojana Is More
content: The scheme is administered by the Women and Child Development Department of Himachal Pradesh, with field implementation carried out through Anganwadi centres and Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS) supervisors at the block level. Anganwadi workers are responsible for identifying newly born girl children in BPL households, informing families about the scheme, and assisting them with the registration process.

To qualify for the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana, the family must hold a BPL ration card or be certified as a Below Poverty Line household by the competent authority; the girl child must have been born in Himachal Pradesh or be a resident of the state and the birth must be registered with the municipal or Gram Panchayat authorities. The registration of the birth is a pre-requisite for the FD opening, making it a secondary incentive for birth registration among rural families.

extra_sections.title: A Deposit Plus Yearly School Support
extra_sections.content:
Beti Hai Anmol gives a Rs 10,000 fixed deposit in the girl's name at birth, which grows with interest until she is older. It also pays annual scholarships through her school years.

The aim is to make families value the girl child and keep her in school, from Class 1 right up to Class 12.

extra_sections.heading: The Birth Deposit
content: The educational scholarship under the scheme requires the girl to be enrolled in a government or government-aided school; private unaided school students are not eligible for the scholarship component, though they may still benefit from the initial FD. This condition is designed to incentivise continued enrolment in schools that are accessible to BPL families, particularly at the secondary level when dropout rates for girls in rural hill areas tend to rise.

Himachal Pradesh has one of the highest female literacy rates among Indian states, and programmes like the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana have contributed to sustaining this achievement by providing direct financial incentives for keeping girl children in school; the scholarship payments are credited annually to the girl's or her parent's bank account on submission of the school's attendance and promotion certificate, creating an incentive for both school attendance and promotion to the next class. This conditional scholarship design links financial support to measurable educational progress.

extra_sections.heading: The Birth Deposit More
content: The scheme has particular relevance in the more remote and economically backward districts of Himachal Pradesh, such as Chamba, Sirmaur, and Kinnaur, where income poverty and the preference for male children can both be higher than in more accessible hill districts; in these areas, the combination of the birth-linked FD and the annual scholarship provides a concrete financial argument for valuing the birth and education of daughters that can be used by Anganwadi workers in community conversations about gender equality. The tangible economic benefit is designed to shift the calculus that can sometimes lead to gender-selective practices.

The Beti Hai Anmol Yojana complements other girl-child-focused national programmes running in Himachal Pradesh, including Beti Bachao Beti Padhao and the Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana (SSY); while SSY is available to all families regardless of economic status, the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana is specifically targeted at BPL households for whom the state makes the initial investment on behalf of the family. The convergence of these programmes creates a multi-layered support system for girls from the most economically vulnerable families.

extra_sections.heading: The Class-wise Scholarships
content: The scholarship amounts are disbursed annually and require the submission of an up-to-date school attendance certificate and proof of promotion to the next class; delays in submission can delay the disbursement for that year, but arrears are settled once the documentation is provided. Anganwadi workers and school teachers are expected to work together to ensure that BPL families are aware of the documentation requirements so that eligible girls do not miss their annual scholarship due to administrative gaps.

HP's Women and Child Development Department maintains a register at the block level of all girls enrolled in the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana, and this register is cross-referenced with school attendance records and Gram Panchayat BPL lists during annual review exercises. Girls who drop out of school before Class 12 stop receiving the scholarship from the year of dropout, but the FD amount continues to be held in the girl's name and can still be withdrawn at age 18 regardless of whether she completed her schooling.

extra_sections.title: Locked in the Girl's Name
extra_sections.desc:
The fixed deposit is opened in the girl child's own name, not the parents', so it is hers when it matures.

This builds a small but real financial base for her future, on top of the yearly scholarships that keep her in school.

extra_sections.heading: The Class-wise Scholarships More
content: The scheme has faced implementation challenges in ensuring that all eligible BPL families in remote hill areas learn about it promptly after the birth of a girl child, as Anganwadi coverage in the highest-altitude villages can be irregular and new parents may not be aware of the scheme without active outreach. The department has addressed this by including Beti Hai Anmol awareness in the maternal and child health counselling sessions that ASHA workers conduct during pregnancy and post-delivery home visits.

The fixed deposit mechanism used by the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana has the advantage of ensuring that the Rs 10,000 grows over the approximately 18 years it is held before the girl can withdraw it; at post office savings or bank FD rates, the matured amount at age 18 can be significantly more than the principal, giving the girl a somewhat larger corpus than the initial deposit. This compounding effect means that even a small initial investment by the government translates into a more meaningful sum by the time the girl reaches adulthood.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible
content: For families in Himachal Pradesh who have girl children with disabilities, the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana benefit is available alongside any disability-specific support they may receive from the Social Justice and Empowerment Department; the eligibility criteria do not exclude disabled girls, and the FD and scholarship are available on the same terms as for non-disabled beneficiaries. Anganwadi workers are trained to identify families with disabled girl children during their regular ICDS surveys and to proactively enrol them in the scheme.

The Beti Hai Anmol Yojana reflects Himachal Pradesh's long-standing investment in gender equity in education and social welfare; the state has consistently ranked well on female education and health indicators, and schemes targeting girl children at the BPL level help ensure that improvements in state-level averages translate to benefits for the most economically excluded families. The scheme's dual focus on the birth event and the educational trajectory ensures that the financial support is sustained across the girl's entire school-going years rather than being a one-time benefit.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible More
content: Parents wishing to enrol their newborn daughter in the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana should contact the nearest Anganwadi centre as soon as possible after birth; the Anganwadi worker will guide them through the registration process and help them obtain the income or BPL certificate and birth registration documents that are needed to open the FD. Early registration ensures that the FD is opened before the one-year window after birth closes, as applications submitted after this period may not be eligible for the birth-linked FD component.

The scheme has also had an indirect impact on birth registration practices in Himachal Pradesh, as the requirement to produce a birth certificate for enrolment has given rural families an added administrative reason to register a girl's birth promptly with the Gram Panchayat; in areas where birth registration was previously incomplete or delayed, the financial incentive of the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana has helped improve registration rates among BPL households. This is a positive externality that strengthens the civil registration infrastructure in rural HP.

extra_sections.title: Stay Enrolled to Keep the Benefit
extra_sections.content:
The scholarship part depends on the girl staying enrolled and attending school each year. Schools and anganwadi workers usually help track this.

Keep your bank and school details updated so each year's scholarship reaches the right account without delay.

extra_sections.heading: How to Apply
content: Social workers and child welfare officers in Himachal Pradesh have observed that the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana creates an occasion for Anganwadi workers to have a positive conversation about daughter birth in BPL households, at a moment when the family is often under financial stress; the news that the government will open a Rs 10,000 FD in the girl's name can help shift the emotional environment surrounding a girl birth in communities where son preference persists. This psycho-social impact of the programme, while difficult to measure directly, may contribute over time to more positive attitudes toward the girl child.

The education scholarship component of the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana is particularly important at the Class 9 to 12 level, where school dropout rates for girls from poor families tend to be highest; the Rs 1,000 to Rs 1,200 annual scholarship at this stage helps offset the cost of textbooks, examination fees, and school uniforms, which are the typical financial barriers that cause families to withdraw their daughters from school at the secondary level. By providing the scholarship precisely at the stages where the economic pressure to drop out is greatest, the scheme supports the critical secondary-to-senior-secondary transition.

extra_sections.text: Beti Hai Anmol Yojana provides a Rs 10,000 fixed deposit at birth and annual scholarships from Class 1 to Class 12 for girl children of BPL families in Himachal Pradesh, creating a financial safety net that grows with the girl from birth to adulthood.

extra_sections.heading: How to Apply More
content: Himachal Pradesh has also integrated the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana into the broader ICDS data systems, so that the beneficiary register maintained at the Anganwadi level can be easily audited by block and district level supervisors during routine monitoring visits. This integration helps prevent both exclusion errors (eligible girls not being registered) and inclusion errors (ineligible families claiming the benefit) at the community level.

The interest earned on the Rs 10,000 FD during the approximately 18-year holding period depends on prevailing post office or bank interest rates; at typical government savings scheme rates of 5 to 7 percent per year, the matured amount at age 18 can range from roughly Rs 20,000 to Rs 30,000, providing the young woman with a meaningful financial asset as she enters adulthood. The fact that this amount is in her own name and under her control at the time of withdrawal reinforces the scheme's goal of promoting women's financial autonomy from the very beginning of their lives.

extra_sections.heading: Documents You Need
content: The Beti Hai Anmol Yojana also serves as a platform for Himachal Pradesh to demonstrate its commitment to the national Beti Bachao Beti Padhao campaign's goals at the state level; the scheme's dual focus on birth support and educational continuity aligns with the campaign's two main pillars of preventing sex-selective practices and keeping girls in school. HP shares data on scheme enrolment and scholarship utilisation with the Ministry of Women and Child Development as part of its annual reporting under the national campaign framework.

Women who received the Beti Hai Anmol benefits as girls and have now turned 18 have begun accessing their matured FD amounts; early anecdotal reports from district welfare offices suggest that many of these young women have used the funds for higher education application fees, vocational training enrollment, or small business setup costs. This pattern of usage validates the scheme's original design intention of providing a resource for the girl's own development choices at the threshold of adulthood rather than channelling the money into family consumption.

extra_sections.title: Documents You Need Notes
extra_sections.content:
The Beti Hai Anmol Yojana is one of several HP state schemes specifically designed to address gender equity at the household level; together with the Indira Gandhi Pyari Behna Sukh Samman Nidhi (monthly income for women aged 18-59) and the HP Widow Pension, it forms part of a continuum of state support that follows women from birth to old age. For BPL families, this lifecycle approach to women's welfare ensures that financial support is available at each critical stage.

District-level data from Himachal Pradesh shows that districts with higher Anganwadi worker coverage and more active ICDS field infrastructure tend to have better enrolment rates in the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana, underscoring the central role of the Anganwadi network in making the scheme work effectively on the ground. The state government has therefore prioritised strengthening ICDS infrastructure in the more remote districts, including filling vacancies for Anganwadi workers and helpers and providing them with updated training on scheme documentation requirements, so that no eligible girl is missed simply due to low Anganwadi density in her village.

extra_sections.heading: Keeping the Scholarships Going
content: For girl children who are orphaned or are in child care institutions, the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana benefit can be claimed by the institution or by the legal guardian on the child's behalf; the FD is still opened in the girl's own name, ensuring that the benefit remains personal to her even in the absence of biological parents. The district child welfare committee oversees the registration of orphaned girl children in welfare schemes including the Beti Hai Anmol programme, and ensures that the girl can access the FD amount when she turns 18 regardless of where she is residing at that time.

faqs.question: What is the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana?
faqs.answer: It is a Himachal Pradesh government scheme that provides a Rs 10,000 fixed deposit at birth and annual scholarships from Class 1 to Class 12 for girl children in Below Poverty Line (BPL) families.

faqs.question: How much is the fixed deposit given at birth?
faqs.answer: A Rs 10,000 fixed deposit is opened in the name of the girl child at birth or within one year of birth. The matured amount can be withdrawn when she turns 18.

faqs.question: Which families are eligible for Beti Hai Anmol Yojana?
faqs.answer: Only BPL (Below Poverty Line) families of Himachal Pradesh are eligible. The family must have a valid BPL ration card or BPL certificate.

faqs.question: How many daughters can benefit from this scheme per family?
faqs.answer: A maximum of two girl children per family are covered under the Beti Hai Anmol Yojana.

faqs.question: What are the annual scholarship amounts?
faqs.answer: Scholarships range from Rs 450 per year in Classes 1-3 to Rs 1,200 per year in Classes 11-12, with increasing amounts at each level through the school years.

faqs.question: When should I register for this scheme after my daughter is born?
faqs.answer: You should contact the Anganwadi worker and apply within one year of the girl's birth to be eligible for the Rs 10,000 fixed deposit component.

faqs.question: Can the scholarship be received if my daughter studies in a private school?
faqs.answer: No. The scholarship component requires the girl to be enrolled in a government or government-aided school. The FD benefit, however, is not conditional on school type.

faqs.question: Where should I apply for Beti Hai Anmol Yojana?
faqs.answer: Contact the Anganwadi worker in your area or visit the block ICDS office. The Anganwadi worker will provide the form and guide you through the registration process.

faqs.question: What documents are needed to apply?
faqs.answer: You need the girl's birth certificate, family BPL ration card or income certificate, parents' Aadhaar cards, Himachal Pradesh domicile certificate, and bank or post office account details.

faqs.question: Can a girl with a disability benefit from Beti Hai Anmol Yojana?
faqs.answer:
Yes. There is no exclusion for disability.

Girl children with disabilities from BPL families are equally eligible for both the FD and the scholarship components.
